BinaryDC.discharge: Pinned exactly, and `maybe` understated what was already proved. `binaryDC_iff_countableBoolChoice` is an equivalence with `CountableBoolChoice`, so this is not a principle awaiting a presentation -- it is countable Boolean choice. The reason is that the hypothesis asks for a decision at every numerator, so every decision precedes the recursion and the walk collapses. Weaker than DC follows rather than being guessed, since DC gives countable choice through `acOmega_of_dc`. What is actually open is strictness -- whether it sits strictly below DC -- which is a question about models that no edge answers, and `BinaryDCOn`'s docstring records it the same way.
BinaryDC.meaning: dependent choice along a two-valued step

DC.discharge: Placed: `dc_of_setChoice` bounds it above and six edges run below it -- `acOmega_of_dc`, `dcOmega_of_dc`, `baire_of_dc`, `baireL_of_dc`, `binaryDCOn_of_dc`, `treeDCZ_of_dc` -- so Baire's dependence on choice along a sequence is registered. The calibration fields are `n/a` by construction: this entry's `principle` is `dc`, so a forward deriving it from itself is not a thing to write, and its placement lives in the lattice.

EM.discharge: never: it is the thing being measured; every use is a deliberate classical reading

FAN\u0394.discharge: Upper bound only. `fanΔ_of_decider` takes a universal decider, which `em` supplies through `decider_of_em`, so `em` implies `FANΔ` along a two-step chain and the forward named here is the second step. Nothing goes the other way: every consumer of `FANΔ` concludes a measure-theoretic statement and none a lattice principle, so its position relative to the omniscience lattice is unmeasured rather than zero. `FANstable` is stronger, not weaker: it demands less of the bar, double-negation stability rather than decidability, and concludes the same, so `fanDelta_of_fanStable` is free in the direction `FANstable -> FANΔ`, and the Weierstrass line is priced at the stronger hypothesis. The reverse `fanΔ -> em` is refuted: the lattice's `_refuted` list carries `fanΔ -> mp` and `fanΔ -> llpo` by the Brouwerian continuity model, and both `llpo` and `mp` lie in the closure of `em`, so `fanΔ -> em` would compose to a refuted edge. The field stays `open` because its vocabulary has no `refuted` value.
FAN\u0394.meaning: a decidable bar is uniform -- the compactness of 2^omega, read constructively

HalveDecider.discharge: Relative to the predicate: a decider for every predicate is refutable, while the sqrt-2 straddle has one outright, spending no principle, so there is no single principle to record. The residue at `straddleSignP G` is the sign of `G` at the midpoint, decided at rational pairs only. Decided implies located and the reverse is the gap: the located form `0 <= G m` or `G m <= 0` is one negation, while the form the construction consumes, `0 <= G m` or its negation, is two.
HalveDecider.meaning: the halving machine's branch is decidable at every step

IsRing.discharge: never: subject matter, not strength -- the ring is the thing under study
IsRing.meaning: the carrier with its operations is a ring

SplitDecision.discharge: never: proved outright. `NumberTheory.Eis.splitDecision` derives it with no hypothesis, so it is not a strength and not a lattice node; the one theorem that takes it as a binder has an unconditional form beside it, and every caller can supply `splitDecision`.
SplitDecision.meaning: every non-zero non-unit Eisenstein integer is irreducible or a product of two non-units --- restricted to non-zero non-units because the unrestricted form is false at a unit, and proved by a bounded box search over candidate factors, so a theorem and not a principle

IsPrime.discharge: never: subject matter, not strength, and at a literal it is a computation rather than an assumption: `isPrime_decidable` decides it through `isPrime_iff_minFac_self`, choice-free at `[propext, Quot.sound]`, so a literal primality proof is `by decide`. No closed binder at a literal remains; the entry stays so that one reappearing is adjudicated here rather than paid. At a variable `p` it is not a closed binder at all.
IsPrime.meaning: a natural number is prime: at least two, and divisible only by one and itself --- decided by `isPrime_decidable` through `isPrime_iff_minFac_self`, so at a literal it is a computation rather than a hypothesis

IsConditionallyCompleteLocated.discharge:
never: the tree proves it outright. `Analysis.isConditionallyCompleteLocated_realL` has no hypotheses at all: the located least-upper-bound property holds constructively, because locatedness is exactly what supplies the rational bracket the supremum is built from. The one binder taking it is a layering artifact, since the discharging theorem sits downstream of the file that takes it.

Not the same object as `IsConditionallyComplete`: this one carries `IsLocatedSubset X lt S` as an extra hypothesis, so it is the weaker property and a descent from it is the stronger result. `Topology.isConditionallyComplete_of_located_of_em` is the bridge and spends `EM` on precisely that gap.
IsConditionallyCompleteLocated.meaning: the least-upper-bound property restricted to located subsets --- the constructively available half, which this tree proves unconditionally at `RealL`

IsMetric.discharge: never: subject matter, not strength -- it takes the very `d` and `X` it constrains and asserts nothing exists, so no principle is hiding in it. It is the ambient structure every metric statement in the tree is stated over, which is why it appears in so many binder lists at once.
IsMetric.meaning: the pair (d, X) is a metric space: d is a RealL-valued function on X x X, nonnegative, vanishing on the diagonal, symmetric, and satisfying the triangle inequality

LLPO.meaning: of two sequences at most one of which fires, one can be named

LPO.discharge: never as a blanket; it is a lattice node and appears only where a reversal pins a theorem to it
LPO.meaning: a binary sequence fires, or never does

ratLt.discharge: never: subject matter, not strength -- a relation between two given rationals, `ratLe r s` together with `r != s`. It carries no existential and no decision the tree does not already have, so a binder taking it asks for an order fact and not for a principle. It reaches `rowbinders.py`'s report only because rationals are ordered in almost every analytic statement here.
ratLt.meaning: strict order on the rationals: ratLe r s and r != s

MP.meaning: Markov: a sequence that cannot be zero everywhere fires

MonotoneConvergence.discharge: Bracketed in the lattice. Both edges are registered: `monotoneConvergence_of_em` bounds it above and `lpo_of_monotoneConvergence` bounds it below, so `em -> monotoneconvergence -> lpo` stands and the node is not one-sided. What is open is narrower: whether LPO alone suffices, which is the forward against this entry's `principle: lpo`. A third route, `monotoneConvergence_of_located`, takes the schema `forall x, x in Real -> Located x` rather than a nullary Prop. That schema is `CutLocated`, which is equivalent to `em`, so the route derives through the `em` edge rather than adding one. It spends its hypothesis at exactly one step, obtaining a member and a non-member of the supremum within `e`; everything before is `seqSup_spec` and everything after is arithmetic. Demanding locatedness at one real per sequence rather than at every real is not a weakening: the constant sequence at any real `x` is monotone and bounded by `x`, its range is `{x}` and its union is `x`, so the schema hands back `Located x` for an arbitrary real. The two are equivalent and the upper bracket stays at EM-strength. The forward reduces to one condition: term-locatedness whose non-member witness misses every term rather than the one it was found at, which under monotonicity is a tail condition. On the staircase family that condition and LPO are equivalent, both directions. That does not discharge the forward: one family is not all sequences, and the staircase is the family the lower bracket was built on.
MonotoneConvergence.meaning: a monotone sequence bounded above converges

PointwiseModulus.discharge: Not a lattice strength in either direction: the gap over ContinuousAtOn is the universe, not a principle. Its own docstring says it -- the modulus is a Lean function on the point, so a proof may evaluate it, and no amount of improving ContinuousAtOn's proof would produce one. continuousAtOn_of_pointwiseModulus forgets it and recovers pointwise continuity, so the carrier is a strengthening rather than a change of subject. Same shape as BoundedLocated over exists_rat_bound; n/a follows FuncGraphs, the existing structural entry with no strength either way
PointwiseModulus.meaning: a per-point modulus of continuity, supplied as a function rather than existentially

SubsetFinite.discharge: no, and it is an equivalence: a subset of a finite set being finite is excluded middle. The registry recorded forward as n/a while subsetFinite_of_em was already proved
SubsetFinite.meaning: a subset of a finite set is finite

TernaryDecidable.discharge: never: lives in _equivalences as a measured strength
TernaryDecidable.meaning: the ternary digit stream of a real is decidable

TernaryLLPO.meaning: the three-way form of LLPO over the ternary digits

TernaryZeroDecidable.meaning: deciding a ternary expansion is zero

UniformlyContinuousOn.discharge: per-function: concrete functions carry a modulus; the blanket form scopes the theory
UniformlyContinuousOn.meaning: a modulus of continuity on the interval

WLPO.discharge: same as LPO: a measurement point, not an assumption to remove
WLPO.meaning: it is identically zero, or is not

_README: The hypothesis inventory: principles the library ASSUMES rather than
proves, threaded through binders instead of axioms. A conditional theorem
is unconditionally provable, so #print axioms sees nothing -- these are
axioms wearing different clothes, and this registry is where each one is
adjudicated. tools/hypotheses.py counts every declaration assuming each
(binder position) and every one concluding in it, and fails on a
registered name that no longer occurs anywhere.
kind: 'principle'  -- a Prop with logical strength (the lattice's kind);
'readout'    -- Type-level data ABOUT an object, demandable of every
object, the cousin of a principle;
'witness'    -- Type-level data supplying an EXISTENTIAL's witness,
where a readout supplies a DISJUNCTION's branch: an
existential withholding a scale against a disjunction
withholding a bit;
'decider'    -- Type-level data carrying a PROMISE about a predicate,
so its strength varies with the predicate and there
may be no single principle to record;
'structural' -- a blanket mathematical hypothesis that scopes a
theory (uniform continuity, detachability).
kind is VALIDATED against exactly these five. It was displayed and never
compared for the registry's whole life, and four entries drifted to a
fifth value nothing defined.
discharge: what removing the hypothesis would take, or why it stays.
calibration: pins the hypothesis to its strength. shape: 'omniscience' |
'choice' | 'modulus' | 'subject'; principle: a lattice node or 'none';
forward: theorem deriving the hypothesis from the principle; reverse:
theorem recovering the principle from the hypothesis schema; 'open' marks
a direction owed, 'n/a' one that does not apply. _uncalibrated counts
entries owing (no block, or an open direction) and must be met exactly.

IsZeroLocator.discharge: Subject matter. `HasZeroLocators`, `forall L U, IsLocated L U -> exists b, IsZeroLocator L U b`, is the node; one locator for one real is not the principle that every located real has one. Possessing a locator costs nothing, so a binder `(hb : IsZeroLocator L U b)` asserts a property of the `b` the caller already has, on the same footing as `IsRing R add mul zero one`. The strength is in the existential: a map choosing a locator for each real implies `WLPO` (Booij, *Extensional constructive real analysis via locators*, MSCS 31(1):64-88, 2021, Lemma 3.10.1).
IsZeroLocator.meaning: a given bit sequence b is a zero locator for the cut (L, U): at every scale it reports the real outside 1/(n+1) or inside 1/n

realLLe.discharge: Subject matter. `def realLLe (a b) : Prop := not (realLLt b a)` is the order relation on located reals: a binder `(h : realLLe x y)` says the caller has handed over two reals in that relation. What costs something is deciding the order at every pair, which is `SignDisjunction`, a node; the property is registered structural so the existential keeps the charge it already carries.
realLLe.meaning: one located real is at most another, as the negation of the strict order

realLLt.discharge: Subject matter. `def realLLt (x y) : Prop := exists p, p in snd x and p in fst y` is the strict order on located reals, and it is positive: a binder supplies a rational separating the two cuts. Supplying one is data the caller has; producing one at an arbitrary pair is the principle, and that is the node, not this.
realLLt.meaning: a rational lies in the upper cut of one located real and the lower cut of another

ratLe.discharge: Subject matter. `ratLe` unfolds to an integer cross-multiplication under representatives, and integer order here is decidable outright -- so not only is the binder a property of supplied data, the quantified form costs nothing either and there is no principle for it to reverse to.
ratLe.meaning: one rational is at most another, via the cross-multiplied integer order

Equinumerous.discharge: Subject matter. `Equinumerous x y := exists f, IsInjection f x y and IsSurjection f x y`. It is an existential and that is not enough to make it a principle: as a hypothesis it says the caller already holds a bijection, which is a witness handed over, not an assertion that one can be found. The claim that carries strength is the one quantifying over sets -- comparability, or a choice of bijection for every pair -- and that is a different statement this head does not make.
Equinumerous.meaning: the caller holds a bijection between the two sets

realLApart.discharge: Subject matter. `realLApart x y := realLLt x y or realLLt y x`. The separation is handed over, including which side: a binder gives the disjunction already resolved, so nothing decides anything here. Getting apartness from a mere inequality is what costs, and that is a separate principle, where the charge belongs.
realLApart.meaning: two located reals are strictly ordered one way or the other, with the side supplied

IsGroup.discharge: never: subject matter, not strength -- the group is the thing under study, exactly as `IsRing` is. It is a `structure . Extends IsMonoid` over the carrier and operations the caller supplies.
IsGroup.meaning: the carrier with its operation and unit is a group

IsPolyOver.discharge: Subject matter. `IsPolyOver R zero f` says `f` is a function on omega into `R` that is eventually `zero`, with the cutoff supplied as part of the hypothesis. The eventual-vanishing clause is an existential over `Nat` whose witness the caller hands over; asking for a cutoff at an arbitrary coefficient sequence would be a search, and no binder of this head performs one.
IsPolyOver.meaning: a coefficient sequence over the ring with a supplied degree bound past which it is zero

IsRingHom.discharge: never: subject matter. `IsRingHom` is three equations about a map the caller supplies -- additive homomorphy, multiplicativity, and the unit -- and asserts the existence of nothing.
IsRingHom.meaning: a supplied map between two rings preserves addition, multiplication and the unit

IsOrderOf.discharge: Subject matter. `IsOrderOf m op e a` fixes `m` as a parameter and asserts minimality of that `m` -- a bounded, decidable condition on data already in hand. The statement that carries weight is that an order exists, which quantifies `m` existentially and is not this head.
IsOrderOf.meaning: a supplied natural number is the least positive exponent returning the element to the unit

Divides.discharge: Subject matter. `Divides d n := exists k, n = d * k` is over `Nat`, where the quotient is bounded by `n` and the search is a decidable finite one -- so even the quantified form is free here and there is no principle to calibrate against.
Divides.meaning: one natural number is a multiple of another

IsIdeal.discharge: never: subject matter, not strength -- the ideal is the thing under study. `IsIdeal I R add mul zero` is containment plus closure clauses about the subset `I` the caller supplies; its one existential is the additive inverse inside `I`, whose witness the hypothesis carries.
IsIdeal.meaning: a supplied subset is closed under addition, contains inverses and absorbs ring multiplication

WithinOf.discharge: Subject matter. `WithinOf z eps := realLLe (realLNeg eps) z and realLLe z eps` is a conjunction of two `realLLe` facts, which is registered structural directly above for the same reason: the window and the point are both supplied.
WithinOf.meaning: a located real lies in the symmetric window of a supplied radius

IsSubring.discharge: never: subject matter, as `IsRing` and `IsIdeal` are. A `structure` of closure clauses about a subset the caller supplies.
IsSubring.meaning: a supplied subset of a ring is itself a ring under the inherited operations

IsFunction.discharge: never: subject matter. `IsFunction f` is single-valuedness of a supplied set of ordered pairs -- a universally quantified equation about data in hand, asserting the existence of nothing.
IsFunction.meaning: a supplied set of ordered pairs is single-valued

IsCancellative.discharge: Subject matter. `IsCancellative R mul zero` is a ring axiom -- multiplication by a non-zero cancels -- quantified over the carrier's own elements and asserting the existence of nothing. It is the premise the fraction field is built over, not a decision procedure: the hypothesis `c /= zero` is handed over at every use, so no apartness is ever decided here.
IsCancellative.meaning: multiplication by a non-zero element of the supplied ring is injective

IsDegOf.discharge: Subject matter. `IsDegOf zero f d` fixes `d` as a parameter and says it is the least bound -- a bounded, decidable condition on data in hand. The strength is in the existential, that a polynomial has a degree, because producing one is what costs. This head asks for a supplied `d` and so asks for strictly less.
IsDegOf.meaning: a supplied natural number is the least bound on a coefficient sequence's support

Close.discharge: Subject matter. `Close x y delta := WithinOf (realLAdd x (realLNeg y)) delta` is `WithinOf` on the difference, and `WithinOf` is registered structural directly above for the same reason: the two points and the radius are all supplied.
Close.meaning: two located reals differ by at most a supplied radius

IsRegularElt.discharge: Subject matter. `IsRegularElt R mul zero a` says the supplied element `a` is a non-zero-divisor -- a universally quantified equation about the carrier, with `a` a parameter and nothing existential. It is the same shape as `IsCancellative` one element at a time.
IsRegularElt.meaning: a supplied ring element annihilates only zero

polyDvd.discharge: Subject matter. `polyDvd R add mul zero e g := exists q, q in PolyRing R zero and g = q * e` is divisibility in the polynomial ring. The existential is a witness handed over by the binder -- the quotient -- not a search the theorem performs; Deciding divisibility at an arbitrary pair would be the principle and no binder of this head asks for it.
polyDvd.meaning: one polynomial is a multiple of another, with the quotient supplied

StableVanishing.discharge: Per carrier, and the tree discharges it at every carrier it uses. `StableVanishing R zero := forall a, a in R -> not a /= zero -> a = zero` quantifies over the carrier, so it is not plain subject matter; the tree proves it outright at each carrier it instantiates, the located reals among them, and where the carrier is abstract `Algebra.stableVanishing_of_decidableVanishing` derives it from the stronger supplied decision. The reverse is `n/a` as a claim about the mathematics: `DecidableVanishing RealL` is floored at `WLPO` while stability holds at `RealL` outright, so no principle is recoverable from this head. `principle` is `none` because the strength varies with the carrier.
StableVanishing.meaning: a doubly negated vanishing is a vanishing, at the supplied carrier

IsLocated.discharge: Subject matter, as `IsZeroLocator` is. `IsLocated L U` is a ten-field `structure` over a supplied cut pair, and its `located` field hands the disjunction `p in L or q in U` over already resolved, so nothing here decides anything. The principle that asserts such a pair exists is a different declaration; registering this head at that node would overcharge every binder, since holding one located real is not the claim that every real is located.
IsLocated.meaning: a supplied pair of rational cuts is a located real

IsIntegralDomain.discharge: never: subject matter, as `IsRing` is -- the domain is the thing under study. A `structure` over the carrier and operations the caller supplies.
IsIntegralDomain.meaning: the supplied carrier with its operations is an integral domain

IsIndep.discharge: Subject matter. `IsIndep R zero vadd smul vzero vs` is linear independence of the supplied list `vs`: a universally quantified implication over coefficient lists of matching length, with no existential and no search. Producing an independent family, or a basis, is what would cost; asserting a supplied list is independent does not.
IsIndep.meaning: a supplied list of vectors admits only the trivial vanishing combination

IsFinite.discharge:
Subject matter. `IsFinite x := exists n, Equinumerous x (ofNat n)` is `Equinumerous` at a natural number, and that head is registered structural above for the reason that decides this one too: as a hypothesis the bijection and the count are handed over, so the existential is a witness the caller holds rather than a claim that one can be found.

That a subgroup of a finite group is finite is excluded middle, and a claim about every subgroup; this head is a property of one supplied set.
IsFinite.meaning: a supplied set is in bijection with a supplied natural number

IsCommMonoid.discharge: never: subject matter, as `IsRing` and `IsGroup` are. A `structure` of the monoid axioms plus commutativity over the carrier the caller supplies.
IsCommMonoid.meaning: the supplied carrier with its operation and unit is a commutative monoid

IsSurjection.discharge: Subject matter. `IsSurjection f x y` is a property of the supplied function `f`: single-valued, with the right domain and range, and hitting every point of `y`. The existential is under a universal and that is the case to watch -- `forall b in y, exists a in x, f a = b` -- but the preimage is read off `f`, which the binder supplies, rather than chosen; what would cost is sectioning it, choosing an `a` for every `b` uniformly, and that is choice and a different statement.
IsSurjection.meaning: a supplied function from one set onto another hits every point of the target

IsInjection.discharge: never: subject matter, the companion of `IsSurjection` above. Universally quantified equations about a supplied function, asserting the existence of nothing.
IsInjection.meaning: a supplied function between two sets identifies no two points

IsPrimeIdeal.discharge: Subject matter. `IsPrimeIdeal I R add mul zero one` ends `forall a b in R, a*b in I -> a in I or b in I`, and a universally quantified disjunction is the shape a principle usually wears. It is the hypothesis that supplies the branch, not the theorem that decides it: a binder of this head hands over a function from the product's membership to the resolved disjunction, and no binder of it searches for which side holds. The statement that would carry strength is that a proper ideal extends to a prime one, which is a different declaration.
IsPrimeIdeal.meaning: a supplied proper ideal is prime, with the branch of the divisibility disjunction supplied

IsModule.discharge: never: subject matter, as `IsRing` and `IsGroup` are. A `structure` of the module axioms over the ring, carrier and scalar action the caller supplies.
IsModule.meaning: the supplied carrier with its addition and scalar action is a module over the supplied ring

IsEquivRel.discharge: never: subject matter. Reflexivity, symmetry and transitivity of a supplied relation, and nothing else.
IsEquivRel.meaning: a supplied relation on a supplied set is an equivalence

IsContentOn.discharge: Subject matter. `IsContentOn R add zero nonneg m A` is six fields about the supplied set function `m` --- functionhood, domain, range, non-negativity, the empty set, and finite additivity on disjoint pairs. Finite is what keeps it structural: the strength of a measure lies in countable additivity, which is carried separately.
IsContentOn.meaning: a supplied set function on a supplied algebra is a finitely additive non-negative content

IsAlgebra.discharge: Subject matter. `IsAlgebra A X` is closure of the supplied family `A` under the finite Boolean operations. The cost sits in closure under countable unions, and the strong-law chain runs over an algebra instead.
IsAlgebra.meaning: a supplied family of subsets is closed under the finite Boolean operations

IsPolyIrreducible.discharge:
Subject matter, and it is the same reading as `IsPrimeIdeal` directly above. `IsPolyIrreducible` ends in a universally quantified disjunction over divisors, and the binder supplies the branch rather than any theorem deciding it.

Deciding reducibility over a field is a different principle, at `em`; charging this head there would overcharge every binder that merely holds an irreducible polynomial.
IsPolyIrreducible.meaning: a supplied polynomial is a non-unit whose divisors are units or associates, with the branch supplied

IsEmbedding.discharge: never: subject matter, the injective case of `IsRingHom` above. Equations and an injectivity clause about a supplied map.
IsEmbedding.meaning: a supplied ring homomorphism is injective

IsBasis.discharge: Subject matter. `IsBasis R zero V vadd vzero smul vs` is spanning plus independence of the supplied list `vs`, and `IsIndep` is registered structural above on the same ground. That every module has a basis is the principle and it is a different statement --- classically it is a choice principle, and no binder of this head makes it, since the list is handed over.
IsBasis.meaning: a supplied list of vectors spans the module and is independent

HasDerivOn.discharge: Subject matter. `HasDerivOn F F' p q` takes the derivative `F'` as a parameter and states the uniform estimate with a modulus the binder supplies --- the same shape as `TendsToL` above, where the value is given and the property asserted of it. Producing a derivative, or a modulus for one, is what would cost.
HasDerivOn.meaning: a supplied function is the derivative of another on the supplied interval, with a modulus

intLe.discharge: Subject matter. `intLe z w := intNonneg (intAdd w (intNeg z))` is the integer order, and integer order is decidable outright in this tree --- so, like `ratLe` above, not only is the binder a property of supplied data, the quantified form costs nothing either and there is no principle for it to reverse to.
intLe.meaning: one integer is at most another

IsSubmodule.discharge: never: subject matter, as `IsSubring` and `IsIdeal` are. Closure clauses about a subset the caller supplies.
IsSubmodule.meaning: a supplied subset of a module is closed under its addition and scalar action

IsSubgroup.discharge:
Subject matter. `IsSubgroup H G op e` is containment plus closure, with the inverse's existential a witness the binder carries.

That a subgroup of a finite group is finite is excluded middle, and quantifies over every subgroup; this head is a property of one supplied subset.
IsSubgroup.meaning: a supplied subset of a group contains the unit and is closed under the operation and inverses

IsMonoid.discharge: never: subject matter, as `IsRing`, `IsGroup` and `IsCommMonoid` are --- and `IsGroup` literally `extends` it.
IsMonoid.meaning: the supplied carrier with its operation and unit is a monoid

IsHom.discharge: never: subject matter, the group-level case of `IsRingHom` above. Equations about a supplied map, asserting the existence of nothing.
IsHom.meaning: a supplied map between two groups preserves the operation

IsCongruence.discharge: never: subject matter. `IsEquivRel` --- registered structural above --- together with compatibility with the operation, both about a relation the caller supplies.
IsCongruence.meaning: a supplied equivalence relation on a group is compatible with its operation

IsAbelian.discharge: never: subject matter --- one equation quantified over the supplied carrier's own elements.

ClosedUnder.discharge: never: subject matter for the first-order semantics. `ClosedUnder D F` says the supplied interpretation `F` keeps the supplied domain `D` closed --- one universally quantified membership fact, with no existential.
ClosedUnder.meaning: a supplied domain is closed under a supplied family of interpreted function symbols

Or.discharge: Subject matter, for the same reason as its neighbour `Not`. A binder `(h : Or P Q)` hands over a proof that names which side holds, since the type is an inductive with `inl` and `inr`; what costs something is being handed the disjunction for every pair of propositions, and that is `logicem`, a registered node carrying six landed outgoing edges.
Or.meaning: this tree's own disjunction, an inductive with two constructors

IsContinuous.discharge: Subject matter. The definition is `IsFunction f` with its domain and range conditions plus the preimage condition: every member of the target topology pulls back into the source one. A binder `(hf : IsContinuous f X Y S T)` says the caller already holds such a function, which is data. The strength in this layer is elsewhere: turning a topological hypothesis into a uniform one is what costs.
IsContinuous.meaning: a function between two spaces pulls every open set back to an open set

IdealEquiv.discharge: Subject matter. The definition is an existential over two non-zero ring elements whose principal multiples of `I` and `J` agree -- the ideal class relation, which is the object the class-group arc studies rather than an assumption about the universe. A binder carrying it hands over the two cofactors. It sits beside the already-registered `IsIdeal` and `IsInvertibleIdeal`, both structural for the same reason.
IdealEquiv.meaning: two ideals agree after multiplication by non-zero principal ideals

OnLine.discharge: Subject matter. `OnLine a b c P` is the single equation `a*x + b*y = c` at a given point, in `realLAdd` and `realLMul` -- nothing quantified, nothing decided.
OnLine.meaning: a point satisfies a line's equation

IsPolyUnit.discharge: Subject matter. `IsPolyUnit` asserts a polynomial inverse exists for a given `p` -- the caller hands over the cofactor. The strength in that neighbourhood is deciding irreducibility, not carrying a factorisation.
IsPolyUnit.meaning: a polynomial has a polynomial inverse

IsUniformBar.discharge: Subject matter, and it is `IsBar`'s conclusion rather than a separate assumption: the same property with the depth bounded. A binder carrying it hands over the bound `N`. What costs is getting from one to the other at a decidable bar, and that is the fan theorem, already a lattice node as `fanΔ`.
IsUniformBar.meaning: a predicate on finite bit strings is met by every infinite path at a bounded depth

IsCauchy.discharge: Subject matter, and it is the textbook case of the property/principle split this registry is built on. Being Cauchy is a property of a supplied sequence and assuming it spends nothing; what costs is the conversion --- extracting a modulus from `forall eps, exists N` over a family is `ACOmega`, and `every Cauchy sequence converges` is the completeness statement. Both of those live at their own nodes. The docstring records only that the statement is one-sided because the other side is the same statement with `m` and `n` swapped, which is a spelling and not a strength.
IsCauchy.meaning: the terms of the sequence eventually differ by less than any positive rational

BinaryDCOnAt.discharge: The lattice node `binarydcon` at one supplied carrier and relation, filed per instance. The quantified form is the node: `dc` reaches it by `binaryDCOn_of_dc`, and `binaryDCOnAt_of_binaryDCOn` is the forward from it to this head. The backward direction does not arise: `halve_limit_of_binaryDCOn` opens the quantified form at a single instance, a set of coded rational intervals, while the universal statement speaks of every carrier including `powerset RealL`; naming the instance is what makes the reversals aimable, as `DCOmega` does for `DCOn`.
BinaryDCOnAt.meaning: dependent choice along a two-valued step, at one supplied carrier and relation

HasDerivAt.discharge: Subject matter, and its `forall n, exists m` is the analytic statement itself rather than a choice: at a single supplied `F`, `a` and `L` a caller discharges it by exhibiting the scale, and the docstring reads it out in those terms --- *for every scale `n` there is a scale `m` such that a point within a rational of `a` has its value within `w/(n+1)` of the linear approximation*. The choice appears one level up and is already priced: turning `forall k, forall n, exists m` into a function over a family of maps is `ACOmega`, a lattice node, and the tree's cheap alternative is the data form, exactly as `LipschitzOn` carries its constant as a parameter. Differentiability at a named point of a named map is none of that.
HasDerivAt.meaning: the map has the supplied derivative at a point of the supplied interval

IsTopIndex.discharge: Subject matter. Two fields about a supplied coefficient function and a supplied index: every coefficient above `d` is zero and the one at `d` is not. The strength in this neighbourhood is finding the top index of an arbitrary polynomial, which needs a zero test on coefficients and is where `DecidableVanishing` enters; this head receives `d` as data and assumes nothing about locating it. The docstring records that `exists_top` witnesses it immediately, so it is inhabited on arrival.
IsTopIndex.meaning: the supplied index is the top nonzero coefficient of the supplied polynomial

realLt.discharge: Subject matter, and it is this tree's own strict order on Dedekind reals, whose docstring prices the classical alternative exactly: *`x subseteq y and x /= y` would not do -- from `x /= y` one cannot produce the rational that separates them without excluded middle*. So the order carries its witness as the definition, and the `em` the subset form would need is the thing avoided. A strict inequality between supplied reals is subject matter at every consumer.
realLt.meaning: some rational lies in the second cut and not the first

realNonneg.discharge: Subject matter. It is `realLe realZero x` under a name, one line and no docstring, so it carries exactly what the non-strict order carries at a supplied real, which is nothing: the non-strict order is the negative, choice-free one, and the omniscience in this area is in comparing two reals, registered at its own nodes.
realNonneg.meaning: the supplied real is at least zero

HasHalveLimit.discharge: Per instance. The bisection machine's conclusion at one supplied predicate, *a real of the unit interval that every stage brackets*, named because three theorems state it. At a single `P` the price depends entirely on `P`: for the sqrt-2 straddle it is free, and other predicates spend `WEM`, or `SignDisjunction` with a `BinaryDCOnAt` instance. A head whose instances range from free to a choice node is the per-instance shape by definition.
HasHalveLimit.meaning: some real of the unit interval is bracketed at every scale by a rational interval satisfying the supplied predicate

ContinuousAtOn.discharge: Subject matter. The docstring says it is `UniformlyContinuousOn` with the second argument pinned: a modulus-style epsilon-delta statement about a supplied function at a supplied point, every quantifier ranging over `Nat` indices and rational widths. Nothing in it decides a real or selects from a family; a caller discharges it by exhibiting the modulus for the function in hand.
ContinuousAtOn.meaning: the supplied function is continuous at one point of a closed interval, in modulus form

Cong.discharge: Subject matter. The docstring states the whole case: *an equation between computed values, so every fact about it is a computation*. An equality of two `Nat` remainders is decidable by evaluation and costs nothing to discharge or to refute.
Cong.meaning: two naturals leave the same remainder modulo n

Dominates.discharge: Subject matter. An injection from one supplied set into another, exhibited. It is the cardinal comparison the file is about, not a principle it spends; the Schroder-Bernstein decisions it would need are registered separately.
Dominates.meaning: some injection maps the first supplied set into the second

Enum.discharge: Subject matter. A supplied `Nat`-indexed family that maps into, injects into and covers a supplied set: an explicit enumeration handed over by the caller, which is exactly what makes a finite product over the set choice-free.
Enum.meaning: the supplied family enumerates the supplied set bijectively by the first n naturals

IsNested.discharge: Subject matter. Two supplied rational sequences are monotone, bracketed and of shrinking width, with the index for each width witnessed. Rational comparisons about supplied data.
IsNested.meaning: the supplied rational sequences form nested intervals of shrinking width

IsSemiring.discharge: Subject matter. The semiring axioms on supplied carrier and operations; every field is an equation or a function fact. The docstring's note that `zeroMul` and `mulZero` are axioms rather than theorems is a statement about the algebra, not a principle.
IsSemiring.meaning: the supplied carrier and operations form a semiring

IsStrictOrderOn.discharge: Subject matter. Irreflexivity and transitivity of a supplied relation on a supplied set. The docstring records why it exists: without it the extreme value theorem over an arbitrary `lt` is false at a one-point example, so this is the order axiom the statement needs, not a principle.
IsStrictOrderOn.meaning: the supplied relation is a strict order on the supplied set

realLe.discharge: Subject matter. The order on Dedekind cuts as inclusion of two supplied cuts; the relation the real line is about.
realLe.meaning: the first supplied cut is contained in the second

straddleSignP.discharge: Subject matter. Two located-real comparisons of a supplied function at two supplied rationals: the payload the bisection carries. The docstring names it so the instance of `BinaryDCOn` can be written, which is the per-instance filing `BinaryDCOnAt` already carries; this head is the predicate, not the choice.
straddleSignP.meaning: the supplied function is nonpositive at a and nonnegative at b

Dvd.discharge: Subject matter. Divisibility in the Eisenstein integers, witnessed by a cofactor; a relation between supplied elements.
Dvd.meaning: the supplied Eisenstein integer d divides the supplied x

HasPath.discharge: Subject matter. A witnessed infinite branch through a supplied tree. The strength lives in the principles that produce a path from a tree condition, which quantify over trees and are lattice nodes; a binder holding one tree's path decides nothing.
HasPath.meaning: some Boolean sequence has every prefix in the supplied tree

HasSum.discharge: Subject matter. Convergence of a supplied series' partial sums to a supplied value, the registered `TendsTo` at `seriesSeq`.
HasSum.meaning: the partial sums of the supplied series converge to S

IdealEquivReg.discharge: Subject matter. The ideal class relation of the registered `IdealEquiv` with both scaling factors regular rather than merely nonzero: an existential over two ring elements whose principal multiples of `I` and `J` agree. A binder carrying it hands over the two cofactors; it is the object the class-group arc studies, not an assumption about the universe.
IdealEquivReg.meaning: two ideals agree after multiplication by principal ideals of regular elements

Iff.discharge: Subject matter. The biconditional connective of the from-axioms logic layer, an inductive bundling two implications between its two argument propositions. A binder of it carries exactly its arguments' content; it is a connective, not a principle.
Iff.meaning: the biconditional connective between two propositions

IsBounded.discharge: Subject matter. A supplied binary tree is empty at some depth. A binder carrying it hands over the depth bound for its tree argument; the principles that turn a tree fact into this bound (the fan-theorem family) are separate lattice nodes, and this predicate only names the property.
IsBounded.meaning: a binary tree has no node at some depth

IsClosed.discharge: Subject matter. A supplied subset has open complement in a supplied topology. A binder carrying it is a fact about its set argument.
IsClosed.meaning: a subset of a topological space is closed

IsCommSemiring.discharge: Subject matter. The commutative-semiring axioms on supplied carrier and operations, beside the already structural ring predicates. A binder carrying it is a fact about its arguments.
IsCommSemiring.meaning: a carrier with operations is a commutative semiring

IsContent.discharge: Subject matter. A supplied function on a supplied family is a nonnegative, empty-null, finitely additive real content. A binder carrying it is a fact about its arguments, beside the structural `IsAlgebra` it is defined over.
IsContent.meaning: a function on a family of sets is a finitely additive content

IsCountablyAdditive.discharge: Subject matter. A supplied content sums over disjoint sequences whose union lies in the family. A binder carrying it is a fact about its content argument.

IsCut.discharge: Subject matter. The Dedekind-cut conditions on a supplied set of rationals. A binder carrying it is a fact about its set argument.
IsCut.meaning: a set of rationals is a Dedekind cut

IsEisenstein.discharge: Subject matter. The Eisenstein data for a supplied candidate factorisation `g h` and a supplied element `d`: both factors are polynomials, divisibility of `g`'s coefficients by `d` is decided index by index, `d` is prime in divisibility form, and `d` does not divide `h`'s constant term. The decidability and primality clauses are about the arguments `d` and `g`, not about every ring, so a binder carrying it is a fact about its data and charges nothing to the universe.
IsEisenstein.meaning: a candidate polynomial factorisation satisfies the Eisenstein conditions at an element

IsFactorization.discharge: Subject matter. A supplied list of primes multiplies to a supplied natural number. A binder carrying it is a fact about its arguments.
IsFactorization.meaning: a list of primes is a factorisation of a natural number

IsInfiniteTree.discharge: Subject matter. A supplied binary tree has a node at every length. A binder carrying it is a fact about its tree argument; the principles that turn this into a path (the Konig and fan family) are separate lattice nodes.
IsInfiniteTree.meaning: a binary tree has a node of every length

IsInnerProduct.discharge: Subject matter. The inner-product axioms for a supplied form on a supplied module, with positivity carried by a supplied set and no totality clause. A binder carrying it is a fact about its arguments.
IsInnerProduct.meaning: a bilinear form on a module is a symmetric positive inner product

IsIrreducible.discharge: Subject matter. A supplied Eisenstein integer is a nonzero nonunit with no nontrivial factorisation. A binder carrying it is a fact about its element argument.

IsLocatedSubset.discharge: Subject matter. A supplied subset of a supplied ordered carrier straddles every ordered pair: some member lies above the lower point or none lies above the upper. It is the per-subset data a located real supplies and an arbitrary subset does not; a binder carrying it is a fact about its subset argument, not an omniscience principle.
IsLocatedSubset.meaning: a subset of an ordered carrier is located at every ordered pair

IsPeano.discharge: Subject matter. A supplied set with a supplied zero and successor satisfies the Peano axioms. A binder carrying it is a fact about its arguments.
IsPeano.meaning: a set with zero and successor is a Peano system

IsRecApprox.discharge: Subject matter. A supplied function on a supplied n obeys the recursion clauses inside n. A binder carrying it is a fact about its function argument.
IsRecApprox.meaning: a function is a finite approximation to a recursion

IsRingNC.discharge: Subject matter. The unital ring axioms, not assumed commutative, for supplied operations on a supplied set. A binder carrying it is a fact about its arguments.
IsRingNC.meaning: a set with operations is a (not necessarily commutative) ring

IsTopology.discharge: Subject matter. A supplied family of subsets of a supplied set satisfies the topology axioms. A binder carrying it is a fact about its family argument.
IsTopology.meaning: a family of subsets is a topology

IsTree.discharge: Subject matter. A supplied predicate on binary strings is prefix-closed. A binder carrying it is a fact about its tree argument.
IsTree.meaning: a predicate on binary strings is a tree

IsUnit.discharge: Subject matter. A supplied Eisenstein integer has a multiplicative inverse. A binder carrying it is a fact about its element argument.
IsUnit.meaning: an Eisenstein integer is a unit

Located.discharge: Subject matter. A supplied cut has a member and a non-member within every positive rational. A binder carrying it is a fact about its cut argument.

PathsDieOut.discharge: Subject matter. Every infinite path leaves the tree T. A binder carrying it is the bar condition on its tree argument; the principle that turns it into a uniform bound is the fan theorem, which is a separate registered node and stays charged where it is spent.
PathsDieOut.meaning: every infinite path leaves a given tree

TendsTo.discharge: Subject matter. f is eventually within every positive rational of L, with witnessed bounds. A binder carrying it is a convergence fact about its sequence and limit.
TendsTo.meaning: a sequence of Dedekind reals tends to L

TendsToZero.discharge: Subject matter. The rational widths w eventually fall below every positive rational. A binder carrying it is a convergence fact about its width sequence.
TendsToZero.meaning: a rational width sequence tends to zero

Ubar.discharge: Subject matter. Every infinite extension of s meets B below one depth bound. A binder carrying it is a uniform-bar fact about its bar and node, which the caller proves for its own B; the fan theorem, which produces it for every bar, is the separately registered `FANΔ` family and is charged where spent.
Ubar.meaning: a finite path is uniformly barred by B

Unbounded.discharge: Subject matter. The subtree of T above s is extendable to every depth. A binder carrying it is a fact about its tree and node.
Unbounded.meaning: the subtree above a node reaches every depth

intNonneg.discharge: Subject matter. z is the class of a pair (a, b) of naturals with b at most a. A binder carrying it is an order fact about its integer.

pairLe.discharge: Subject matter. Inclusion of two sets. A binder carrying it is an order fact about its arguments.
pairLe.meaning: one lower cut is contained in another

JunkOk.discharge: never: subject matter, not strength -- the binder says the derivation context lists the seven junk-set axioms, which is a membership fact about a `List Formula` and carries nothing about the universe.
JunkOk.meaning: the first-order context contains every junk-set axiom
